issues.description: The template Lecture.java declares a constructor with only three parameters (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents), but the problem statement requires a constructor that initializes all five attributes in the UML order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implements a five-parameter constructor. The existing three-parameter constructor in the template may confuse students or lead them to implement the wrong signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template constructor in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to the five-parameter signature matching the UML and instructions: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) { ... } or remove the partial constructor stub entirely so students add the correct constructor themselves. Ensure the parameter order follows the UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors).
